findings.detail: Critical Metals Corp (NASDAQ: CRML, NY-based) acquired Tanbreez deposit, potentially world largest rare earth deposit. Received $120M EXIM Bank LOI (June 2025) under Supply Chain Resiliency Initiative for 15-year term loan. Also secured $50M PIPE from unnamed institutional investor. Total project capex ~$290M. Tanbreez contains tantalum, niobium, rare earths, and zirconium on a 4.7B tonne mineralized kakortokite unit. 30-year exploitation license valid to 2050. DFS expected end 2025. The EXIM loan represents US government financial commitment to Greenland mineral extraction.

Resolution: March 5 2026, GEM Agreement terminated the SPA. GEM received 1,409,624 shares (warrant exercise) + 2,744,062 shares for no consideration (settlement). CRML files registration for 2.744M resale shares.

CRML purchased 40kg of ultra-high-purity copper powder from this Swiss company in exchange for 2,000,000 ordinary shares (valued by both parties at $20,000,000 = $10/share). Issuer explanation is that this gives CRML tangible commodity assets. Swiss Commodity Re Limited is unidentified - no prior appearance in CRML filings. Related party or arm's-length transaction unclear.

SYNTHESIS: CRML is a BVI-incorporated, pre-revenue rare earth shell with going concern doubt that has become the primary vehicle for US government-backed Greenland mineral extraction. Key network connections: (1) Cornerstone Government Affairs lobbied for BOTH CRML and Anduril — shared firm with SVDG-affiliated lobbyist Schnappauf bridging defense-tech and mining. (2) Cantor Fitzgerald owns CRML shares via Sizzle SPAC underwriting; Howard Lutnick (Commerce Sec) was indirect owner until May 2025 divestiture to sons — active Senate conflict-of-interest scrutiny. (3) Michael Ryan (former DDASD NATO/European Policy) placed on CRML board March 2025, coinciding with EXIM LOI pursuit. (4) GreenMet brokered the Tanbreez deal but is COMPLETELY ABSENT from 167 SEC filings — compensation structure deliberately kept off public record. (5) European Lithium (Tony Sage parent) selling down from 84% to 37% extracting $200M+ while CRML has $7.3M cash and $52M annual losses. (6) $50M PIPE investor is Alyeska Master Fund (Chicago, 9.9% holder, $70M+ total). (7) Swiss Commodity Re: mysterious $20M copper powder purchase — possible dilution vehicle. (8) Former Greenland Deputy Minister Schonwandt drafted mining law now consulted by Tanbreez — regulatory capture. The overall picture: a financially precarious BVI shell with Trump-network board placement, shared defense-tech lobbying infrastructure, and a deliberately opaque intermediary (GreenMet) channeling US government financing to Greenland rare earths.

SYNTHESIS (Wave 4): Two vectors deepened. (1) RTSKHILADZE-ASBESTOS: Giorgi Rtskhiladze (Mueller Report figure, Toroil/Silk Road CIS network) paid $1.2M to Javelin for EPA chrysotile lobbying Q3 2025. No FARA registration. Russian/Kazakh chrysotile producers (Uralasbest/Kostanai, 68% global output) are primary beneficiaries of ban delay. OxyChem was sole US importer from Brazil/China — Russia/Kazakhstan would be next source post-Brazil ban. FARA hypothesis structurally plausible but no direct Rtskhiladze-producer link found. Javelin's Q3 2025 client roster is a CIS geopolitical cluster: Ukraine tech (Capstone), Russian-linked asbestos (Logical Strategies), critical minerals (NioCorp). (2) I-MEI/SAGE: I-MEI Foods Taiwan cluster confirmed as tightly controlled by chairman Chih Shang Kao (also runs Golden Saddle drone factory). Chelpis Quantum has genuine NIST PQC credentials. Targeting DoD contracts under NDAA Taiwan drone provision. Tony Sage portfolio fully mapped: CRML/EUR(39.5% of CRML)/CuFe/Cape Lambert/Okewood hub. AFP Operation Lemans allegations (bribery, insider trading, offshore loans) unresolved since 2012.

curation.lead:
Critical Metals Corp (NASDAQ: CRML) is a British Virgin Islands-incorporated, pre-revenue mining company that holds the Tanbreez rare earth deposit in southern Greenland [Finding #6260]. Formed through a February 2024 SPAC merger underwritten by Cantor Fitzgerald [Finding #6251], the company received a Letter of Interest from the US Export-Import Bank in June 2025 for up to $120 million in financing [Finding #6246]. As of June 30, 2025, CRML reported losses of $51.9 million for the fiscal year and $7.3 million in cash, with auditors citing substantial going-concern doubt [Finding #6262].

CRML's shareholder structure links it to several figures in US government and finance. Howard Lutnick, the US Commerce Secretary and former Cantor Fitzgerald CEO, held an indirect interest through SPAC underwriting shares [Finding #6269]. CEO Tony Sage controls the company through European Lithium, which reduced its stake from 58.9% to 37.3% between June 2025 and February 2026 while receiving at least $54.75 million in secondary sales [Finding #6273]. The company retained Cornerstone Government Affairs for $210,000 in lobbying and registered on SAM.gov with former Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense Michael Ryan as the government point of contact [Finding #6240][Finding #6245].
curation.system_role: Critical Metals Corp is a BVI-incorporated, pre-revenue mining company seeking US government financing for rare earth extraction in Greenland, structured across multiple jurisdictions (BVI holding company, Australian parent, Greenland asset, US listing) with connections to the US Commerce Secretary and former defense officials.

sections.title: Corporate Structure and SPAC Origins
sections.content:
Critical Metals Corp was incorporated in the British Virgin Islands in October 2022, with its registered address at Maples Corporate Services in Tortola and its business address at 32 Harrogate Street, West Leederville, Australia [Finding #6260]. The company originated as Sizzle Acquisition Corp (NASDAQ: SZZLU), a special purpose acquisition company that raised its IPO in November 2021 with Cantor Fitzgerald as underwriter [Finding #6251]. Sizzle merged with European Lithium Ltd (ASX: EUR) to form CRML, which began trading on February 28, 2024, with EUR receiving approximately 80% of the combined entity [Finding #6251]. Cantor Fitzgerald received 1,247,250 shares as compensation: 1,200,000 as a deferred underwriting fee and 47,250 from a private placement at a deemed issue price of $0.79 per share [Finding #6269].

The company files as a foreign private issuer (20-F) with the SEC under CIK 0001951089 [Finding #6260]. Its SAM.gov registration lists UEI XW4PVY32Q7K1 and CAGE code KD8P2, with a physical address in Winchester, United Kingdom, and a country of incorporation of the British Virgin Islands [Finding #6245]. The board identified a significant deficiency in internal controls, stating that the company lacks controls to ensure accurate and complete accounting for related-party transactions due to a lack of personnel [Finding #6278].

sections.title: Tanbreez Rare Earth Acquisition
sections.content:
The Tanbreez rare earth deposit in southern Greenland is CRML's primary asset, holding a 30-year exploitation license valid to 2050 [Finding #6106]. The deposit sits on a 4.7 billion tonne mineralized kakortokite unit containing tantalum, niobium, rare earths, and zirconium [Finding #6106]. CRML acquired its interest through a multi-stage transaction with Rimbal Pty Ltd, an Australian company controlled by geologist Gregory Barnes (47 Labouchere Road, South Perth) [Finding #6264]. On June 5, 2024, CRML signed a Heads of Agreement, acquiring 5.55% for $5 million in cash on June 18, 2024, followed by an additional 36.45% (Stage 1) on July 23, 2024, in exchange for approximately 8.4 million CRML shares valued at roughly $90 million [Finding #6275].

A make-whole provision triggered on April 28, 2025, awarding Rimbal an additional 5 million shares at $1.37 per share due to share price decline [Finding #6275]. On September 29, 2025, the Heads of Agreement was amended to remove the original $10 million exploration spending requirement, instead obligating CRML to issue 14.5 million shares to Rimbal for Stage 2, which would bring total ownership to 92.5% pending Greenland government approval [Finding #6275]. Rimbal participated as a selling shareholder in the October 2025 PIPE, disposing of 2 million shares to Alyeska Master Fund at $7 per share for $14 million [Finding #6264]. GreenMet brokered the Tanbreez partnership but does not appear in any of CRML's SEC filings, and the compensation structure for this intermediary role remains undisclosed [Finding #6271].

sections.title: Key Relationships and Network
sections.content:
Howard Lutnick, who became US Commerce Secretary in January 2025, held an indirect interest in CRML through Cantor Fitzgerald's 1,247,250 SPAC underwriting shares [Finding #6269]. Cantor Fitzgerald received these shares as a deferred underwriting fee and private placement from the November 2021 IPO, and subsequently reduced its holdings [Finding #6269].

GreenMet brokered CRML's partnership with the Tanbreez project and facilitated the EXIM Bank LOI process, but the firm is absent from CRML's 167 SEC filings [Finding #6271]. Cornerstone Government Affairs registered as CRML's lobbyist in February 2025, deploying five lobbyists including Matt Schnappauf across defense, trade, manufacturing, and foreign relations issue areas [Finding #6240]. According to disclosure filings, the lobbying engagement terminated in October 2025, approximately four months after the EXIM LOI was issued [Finding #6248]. Michael Ryan, a former Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for European and NATO Policy (October 2019 to October 2020) and retired USAF Colonel, joined the CRML board and was listed as the government point of contact on the SAM.gov registration [Finding #6277][Finding #6245].

sections.title: Financial Architecture and Capital Raises
sections.content:
CRML reported losses of $51.9 million in fiscal year 2025 and $139.4 million in fiscal year 2024, with net cash outflows from operations of $14.5 million and only $7.3 million in cash on hand as of June 30, 2025 [Finding #6262]. European Lithium Ltd, the controlling shareholder, provided capital contributions totaling $45.7 million to CRML and its subsidiaries as of the same date, with an additional $5.85 million balance owed [Finding #6278]. As of June 30, 2025, EUR held 62.9 million shares (58.9%), while Rimbal Pty Ltd held 11.7 million shares (11%) [Finding #6263]. No named director or officer reported greater than 1% direct beneficial ownership [Finding #6270].

The company has executed multiple capital raises since listing. In February 2025, CRML issued 4.91 million shares and warrants for $24.55 million to 29 accredited investors, with brokerage by Jett Capital Advisors, J.V.B. Financial Group, and EAS Advisors [Finding #6267]. The largest single investment came from Alyeska Master Fund LP of Chicago, which deployed approximately $85 million across two October 2025 PIPE tranches: $35 million for 5 million new shares plus warrants, and $50 million for an additional 1.47 million shares plus pre-funded warrants [Finding #6261]. Alyeska also purchased 3 million shares from EUR for $21 million and 2 million from Rimbal for $14 million in the same transactions [Finding #6265]. Empery Asset Management, an early post-SPAC investor, reduced its position from 9.23% in September 2024 to 1.97% by June 2025 [Finding #6266].

EUR reduced its stake from 58.9% to 37.3% between June 2025 and February 2026, extracting at minimum $54.75 million through secondary sales to Alyeska [Finding #6273]. In January 2026, EUR sold 5 million shares under Rule 144 for approximately $85.5 million in gross proceeds [Finding #6268]. The board approved $26.9 million in aggregate compensation to directors and executive officers for fiscal year 2025, including 2.11 million ordinary shares issued as equity awards in July 2025 [Finding #6276].

sections.title: Government Financing and Federal Registration
sections.content:
On June 16, 2025, the US Export-Import Bank issued a Letter of Interest to CRML for up to $120 million in financing for the Tanbreez project, under a 15-year term through the Supply Chain Resiliency Initiative within the China and Transformational Exports Program [Finding #6246]. The LOI is not a formal loan commitment; EXIM stated only that it would consider financing [Finding #6246]. Total project capital expenditure is estimated at approximately $290 million, with the definitive feasibility study expected by the end of 2025 [Finding #6106].

CRML registered on SAM.gov on October 13, 2025, with an activation date of October 15 and a registration purpose of Z2 (federal contracts and grants) [Finding #6245]. The primary NAICS code is 212290, Other Metal Ore Mining [Finding #6245]. Analysis of the registration timing identified that it occurred six days after the Cornerstone lobbying engagement terminated on October 7, 2025 [Finding #6248]. Cornerstone's lobbying issue descriptions evolved from initial defense and science focus to include trade, manufacturing, and budget appropriations, with the stated objective of advocacy for US government partnerships to secure and process critical minerals domestically [Finding #6241].

sections.title: Discontinued Strategies and Non-Core Transactions
sections.content:
On January 21, 2025, CRML announced adoption of Bitcoin as its primary treasury asset and entered a $500 million senior convertible note purchase agreement with an unnamed lead investor, with an initial closing of $100 million planned [Finding #6272]. The notes were convertible at $6.00 per share with warrants at $7.00, and the Bitcoin purchase was conditioned on the company's market capitalization exceeding $820 million [Finding #6279]. The agreement was terminated on October 3, 2025, as a condition of the Alyeska PIPE closing, and the strategy was never executed [Finding #6272].

On November 25, 2025, CRML entered an Asset Sale Agreement with Swiss Commodity Re Limited, purchasing 40 kilograms of ultra-high-purity copper powder in exchange for 2 million ordinary shares valued at $20 million ($10 per share) [Finding #6281]. Swiss Commodity Re Limited had no prior appearance in CRML filings, and whether the transaction was arm's-length or related-party remains undisclosed [Finding #6281]. Separately, CRML entered a $125 million draw-down facility with GEM Global Yield LLC SCS in July 2023, which led to an arbitration dispute when GEM exercised warrant rights demanding $27.2 million in shares in February 2025 [Finding #6280]. The dispute was resolved in March 2026, with GEM receiving 1.41 million shares from warrant exercise plus 2.74 million shares for no consideration as settlement [Finding #6280].

sections.title: Board Composition and Personnel
sections.content:
Tony Sage serves as CEO and Executive Chairman, having held the position since April 2024, and controls CRML through European Lithium, which retains investor rights to nominate four of five directors while holding more than 50% of shares [Finding #6277]. The remaining leadership includes CFO Sergey Savchenko, CTO George Karageorge, General Counsel John Thomas, and IR officer Thomas McNamara [Finding #6199]. As of fiscal year 2025, no director or officer reported direct beneficial ownership exceeding 1%, with Sage's interest held indirectly through European Lithium [Finding #6270].

The board includes Mykhailo Zhernov, managing partner of Millstone & Co Investment Company in Ukraine and former founder of ALTERA FINANCE [Finding #6277]. Zhernov sold 500,000 shares under Rule 144 on October 31, 2025, for approximately $628,270 [Finding #6268]. Michael Hanson, a partner at Hanson Peak LLP with 30 years in natural resources and corporate finance including postings in Russia and South Africa, chairs the Audit Committee [Finding #6277]. Michael Ryan, the former Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for European and NATO Policy (October 2019 to October 2020) and 25-year USAF veteran who graduated from the French War College and National Intelligence University, joined the board and was listed as the government POC on the SAM.gov registration [Finding #6277][Finding #6245].

open_questions: What is the compensation structure between GreenMet and CRML for brokering the Tanbreez partnership, given GreenMet's complete absence from 167 SEC filings?
Who is Swiss Commodity Re Limited, and what is the commercial rationale for exchanging $20 million in equity for 40kg of copper powder?
Has the EXIM Bank LOI progressed to a formal loan commitment, and what conditions or due diligence findings have emerged from the feasibility study expected in late 2025?
What is the relationship, if any, between Michael Ryan's former DoD role in European/NATO policy and his placement on the board of a company seeking US government financing for a Greenland asset?
Who was the unnamed lead investor in the abandoned $500 million Bitcoin convertible note agreement, and was there any connection to parties in the existing CRML shareholder network?
